facts.fact_text: The assembly was scheduled to take place from 6.30 to 8.30 p.m. on Thursday, 4 September 2003.
On 4 September 2003 a few dozen residents gathered on the Zashchitnikov Neba Square.
The applicant was among the residents who gathered on the Zashchitnikov Neba Square on 4 September 2003.
The police dispersed the crowd at the Zashchitnikov Neba Square on 4 September 2003 by force.
According to the administrative-arrest record of 4 September 2003, the applicant was arrested for refusing to comply with a lawful order of the police.
Following the applicant's complaints about unlawful police actions, the Kuntsevskiy District Prosecutor interviewed the officers who had apprehended the applicant.
Captain F., Officer D. and the driver L. stated that they had been present at the assembly site since 6 p.m. on 4 September 2003.

Captain F., Officer D. and the driver L. stated that at 8 p.m. on 4 September 2003, when people were beginning to leave, they had arrested the applicant and taken him to the police station "for clarification of facts, namely the [legal] ground for holding a public assembly".

Mr N., who had been the duty officer at Krylatskoye district police station, testified that at 8 p.m. on 4 September 2003 the head of the police station had told him to prepare a report on an administrative offence of disobedience of police orders committed by Mr Makhmudov (the applicant), who had been "detained for conducting an unauthorised meeting".
At Krylatskoye district police station the applicant was placed in a cell.
The applicant remained in the cell at Krylatskoye district police station until he was brought before a judge on 5 September 2003.
The cell at Krylatskoye district police station was dirty and covered with spittle.
The applicant was not given any food or drink while detained at Krylatskoye district police station.

Under Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, organisers of an assembly were required to serve written notice on the municipal authorities no later than ten days before the planned assembly (§ 2).
Under Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, the municipal authority was required to give its response no later than five days before the assembly (§ 3).

Under Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, an assembly could be banned if its purpose was contrary to the Constitution or threatened public order or the security of citizens.

The provisional regulations on the procedure for notification of the executive branch of the Moscow authorities about meetings, street marches, demonstrations and pickets in streets, squares and other public places were approved by Presidential Decree no. 765 of 24 May 1993.

Under the provisional regulations approved by Presidential Decree no. 765 of 24 May 1993, notice of an assembly was to be served by the assembly organisers on the executive body between the fifteenth and tenth day before the planned assembly (§ 2).

Under the provisional regulations approved by Presidential Decree no. 765 of 24 May 1993, the executive body could refuse to accept the notice if the purpose of the assembly was contrary to the principles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, generally accepted public morals, if there was no undertaking on the part of the organisers to ensure public safety, if the assembly coincided in time and place with another one, if it threatened normal functioning of companies or organisations, or if it required suspending public or rail transport (§ 4).

Under the provisional regulations approved by Presidential Decree no. 765 of 24 May 1993, the executive body, in cooperation with the organisers, could suggest a different place, time or route of the assembly in order to ensure public safety (§ 5).
Under the provisional regulations approved by Presidential Decree no. 765 of 24 May 1993, refusal to accept notice of an assembly was amenable to judicial review (§ 10).
The Suppression of Terrorism Act (Federal Law no. 130-FZ of 25 July 1998) was in force at the material time.

Under the Suppression of Terrorism Act (Federal Law no. 130-FZ of 25 July 1998), the Ministry of the Interior fought terrorism by way of preventing, detecting and putting an end to terrorist offences pursuing lucrative goals (section 7 § 3).

Under the Suppression of Terrorism Act (Federal Law no. 130-FZ of 25 July 1998), regional executive bodies, municipal bodies, public associations and organisations and State officials were required to assist the authorities responsible for suppression of terrorism (section 9 § 1).

Under Article 27.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, administrative arrest — a temporary restriction of liberty of an individual — may be ordered in exceptional circumstances where it is necessary for a correct and prompt examination of the administrative case.

Under Article 27.5 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, the duration of administrative arrest must not exceed three hours, except for situations described in paragraphs 2 and 3 of that Article.

Under Article 27.5 § 3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, anyone who is subject to administrative proceedings concerning an offence punishable by administrative detention may be placed under administrative arrest for a period not exceeding forty-eight hours.

Under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, disobedience of a lawful order or demand of a police officer is punishable by an administrative fine or by up to fifteen days' administrative detention (administrativnyi arest).

Under Article 1070 § 1 of the Civil Code, the State or regional treasury is liable — irrespective of any fault by State officials — for damage sustained by an individual on account of unlawful criminal prosecution, unlawful application of a preventive measure in the form of placement in custody or an undertaking not to leave the place of residence, or an unlawful administrative penalty in the form of detention or community work.

The prefect cancelled his decision of 29 August 2003 "in connection with the operative information of law-enforcement authorities about an expected outbreak of terrorist activities in the Krylatskoye district and with a view to ensuring the safety of the district's residents".

In the letter of 2 September 2003, the head of the police command of the Western Administrative District asked the prefect to annul his decision of 29 August 2003 because the police command "had received, from various sources, information about potential terrorist attacks in Moscow, in places of mass gatherings".
